run.answer:
# Research Report: L1HS Transposable Element

## Question Scope
This report examines the L1HS transposable element across five dimensions: sequence, genomic location, expression, disease associations, and supporting literature evidence. The goal is to inventory the available evidence, assess its quality, and synthesize a concise answer while transparently noting limitations and gaps.

## Evidence Inventory
Evidence was gathered from eight plugins—Entity Resolver, Literature, Literature Reading, Graph, Expression, Genome, Sequence, and Citation Resolver—producing 36 claims supported by 36 evidence items and 377 citations. Claim-level support is summarized below, grouped thematically with inline references.

### Entity Resolution
The TE entity L1HS was resolved with two strict aliases (L1HS, L1HS‑Ta) at confidence 0.93 (evidence_1).

### Sequence Information
L1HS maps to a Repbase‑backed consensus sequence of 6064 bp with structural hints including LTR and LINE (evidence_35; Repbase references by Smit et al. 1995 and Jurka & Gentles 2005).

### Genomic Location
A representative genomic locus on chromosome 1 (chr1:231646101‑231652225, minus strand, length 6124 bp) was identified, with 1620 total genomic hits (evidence_34).  
*Note: This is a representative region; L1HS is a multicopy element with numerous genomic copies.*

### Expression Profiles
Top expression contexts are: normal tissue – prostate gland (evidence_31); normal cell line – foreskin fibroblast (evidence_32); cancer cell line – anaplastic large cell lymphoma (evidence_33). These derive from precomputed aggregated expression data, not raw experimental measurements.

### Literature Evidence

#### Transcription Regulation
Human L1 retrotransposon transcription is regulated by its promoter and influenced by transcription factors and environmental agents (evidence_8; high). This integrates findings from multiple studies:
- An antisense promoter within L1 drives transcription of adjacent cellular genes (PMID 11238933).
- The human LINE‑1 promoter was identified and characterized with cell‑type specificity (PMID 1701022).
- The transcription factor RUNX3 plays a role in L1 transcription and retrotransposition (PMID 12907736).
- Steroid hormone‑like agents affect L1 transcription (PMID 11971989).

#### DNA Methylation and Silencing
Young L1 elements undergo DNA methylation, contributing to their silencing (evidence_9; medium). This is supported by a genome‑wide methylation profiling method for young L1 elements (bs‑ATLAS‑seq; PMID 36449162).

#### Cell‑Type and Locus Restriction
L1 activation and retrotransposition are restricted to specific cell types and permissive genomic loci (evidence_10; medium). The seminal study (PMID 27016617) shows that activation of individual L1 instances is cell‑type and locus dependent.

#### Off‑Target Retrieval
The PubMed search also returned a murine study (PMID 9714732) on tissue‑specific expression of a G‑protein‑coupled receptor; its relevance to human L1HS is minimal and it is noted only for completeness.

### Disease Links (Graph Plugin)
The internal knowledge graph associates L1HS with multiple diseases (all rated “high” support). Selected associations with representative supporting PMIDs are listed below; each claim is backed by multiple citations from the graph.

| Disease Association | Evidence ID | Representative PMID(s) |
|---------------------|-------------|------------------------|
| Cancer (somatic mobilization contributes to cancer) | evidence_11 | 22968929, 25352549 |
| Carcinoma (escape from DNA methylation, activity in carcinomas) | evidence_12 | 22968929 |
| Colorectal cancer (excessive mutagenesis by human‑specific L1) | evidence_13 | 22968929 |
| Disturbed spermatogenesis (hypomethylation detected) | evidence_14 | 38759652 |
| Genetic disease (L1 activity has potential to cause disease) | evidence_15 | 25352549 |
| Genetic disease (retrotransposition occasionally leads to human genetic disorders) | evidence_16 | 25352549 |
| Lung cancer (LINE‑1 hypomethylation in circulating DNA, L1Hs‑family specific) | evidence_17 | 27565927 |
| Lung squamous cell carcinoma (highest L1HS expression) | evidence_18 | 41681929 |
| Neural tube defect (L1Hs hypomethylation in neuronal tissues) | evidence_19 | 26122653 |
| Non‑small cell lung cancer (hypomethylation assessed in circulating DNA) | evidence_20 | 27565927 |
| Schizophrenia (L1HS transpositions as genomic risk factor) | evidence_21 | 26990047 |
| Systemic lupus erythematosus (L1Hs loci transcriptionally active in SLE neutrophils) | evidence_22 | 37165451 |

### Gene Interactions (Graph Plugin)
The graph also captures L1HS integration events and regulatory effects on specific genes, predominantly from colorectal tumor studies.

| Gene Relationship | Evidence ID | Representative PMID(s) |
|-------------------|-------------|------------------------|
| CDH11 – targeted by somatic LINE‑1 insertions in colorectal tumors | evidence_23 | 22968929 |
| CHRM3 – L1HS provides a novel promoter | evidence_24 | 19669628 |
| CHRM3 – L1HS integrated into the CHRM3 gene | evidence_25 | 19669628 |
| Genes associated with neural functions/disease – preferential integration | evidence_26 | 29327725 |
| ODZ3 – targeted by somatic LINE‑1 insertions in colorectal tumors | evidence_27 | 22968929 |
| PCM1 – targeted by somatic LINE‑1 insertions in colorectal tumors | evidence_28 | 22968929 |
| PTPRM – targeted by somatic LINE‑1 insertions in colorectal tumors | evidence_29 | 22968929 |
| ROBO2 – targeted by somatic LINE‑1 insertions in colorectal tumors | evidence_30 | 22968929 |

## Citation Assessment
The majority (21 of 23) of the deduplicated citation records have PubMed identifiers, enabling verification. Several citations originate from a “local_graph” source without full metadata (e.g., missing year, journal), which limits independent assessment of their timeliness and context. No unsupported claims were detected; every claim links to at least one piece of evidence. However, many citations are reused across multiple claims because plugins forward citation bundles from a common upstream source, which slightly inflates the count without adding independent support. The literature search query, ““L1HS” AND “expression” AND “sequence”,” captured a reasonable set of studies, though it may have missed relevant literature not indexed under those terms.

## Gaps
The following limitations and evidence gaps are noteworthy:

1. **Sequence:** Only a Repbase consensus is available; the actual genomic copies may vary, and no alignment data are provided.
2. **Genomic Location:** The representative locus is just one of 1620 hits; comprehensive coordinates and copy‑specific annotations are absent.
3. **Expression:** Expression data come from precomputed aggregated profiles, not raw experimental values, and the provenance (e.g., RNA‑seq datasets) is not specified.
4. **Disease Associations:** Derived from an internal knowledge graph that may not be exhaustive or fully current; the underlying studies were not individually screened for quality.
5. **Literature Coverage:** The PubMed search retrieved a murine study (PMID 9714732) with limited relevance to human L1HS, and important papers may have been missed due to the specific query used.
6. **Support Strength:** Plugin‑assigned support strengths (high/medium) are automated and should be interpreted cautiously; medium‑strength claims (e.g., methylation profiling) rely on single papers.
7. **Citation Quality:** Several citations lack complete bibliographic metadata, and two Repbase references lack PubMed identifiers, reducing traceability.

## Answer
Based on the assembled evidence, L1HS is a human‑specific LINE‑1 retrotransposon with a 6064 bp consensus sequence and thousands of genomic copies, exemplified by a locus on chromosome 1. Its expression is highest in prostate tissue, foreskin fibroblasts, and anaplastic large cell lymphoma cells, though these are aggregated profiles with limited granularity. Transcription is driven by its own promoter, modulated by transcription factors (e.g., RUNX3) and environmental agents; an antisense promoter can affect adjacent genes. DNA methylation silences young L1 elements, and activation is both cell‑type and locus‑restricted.

L1HS mobilization is implicated in multiple diseases, notably cancer (especially colorectal and lung cancers), disturbed spermatogenesis, neural tube defects, schizophrenia, and systemic lupus erythematosus. Somatic insertions into genes such as CDH11, CHRM3, ODZ3, PCM1, PTPRM, and ROBO2 have been documented in colorectal tumors, and L1HS can even donate a novel promoter to CHRM3. Substantial evidence gaps remain: the sequence consensus may not reflect all genomic variants; expression data are crude; disease associations need independent validation; and the literature capture may be incomplete. Overall, the evidence supports a role for L1HS as an active, regulated retrotransposon with significant disease relevance, but precise mechanisms and disease‑specific consequences require further study.

normalized_findings: PubMed search with query '"L1HS" AND "expression" AND "sequence"' yielded 21 candidates, of which 8 were reviewed and carried forward.

All references are external (PubMed); no local database matches were found.
Literature evidence can support sections on L1 transcription and regulation but will require full-text reading for detailed expression or sequence data.

walk_steps.summary: Resolved the TE entity L1HS with 2 strict alias variants.
Searched PubMed with the query ""L1HS" AND "expression" AND "sequence"".
Literature evidence includes "Antisense promoter of human L1 retrotransposon drives transcription of adjacent cellular genes." (PMID 11238933).
Literature evidence includes "Identification, characterization, and cell specificity of a human LINE-1 promoter." (PMID 1701022).
Literature evidence includes "Genome-Wide Young L1 Methylation Profiling by bs-ATLAS-seq." (PMID 36449162).
Literature evidence includes "Activation of individual L1 retrotransposon instances is restricted to cell-type dependent permissive loci." (PMID 27016617).
Literature evidence includes "Molecular characterization and tissue-specific expression of a murine putative G-protein-coupled receptor." (PMID 9714732).
Human L1 retrotransposon transcription is regulated by its promoter and influenced by transcription factors and environmental agents.
Young L1 elements are subject to DNA methylation, which plays a role in their silencing.
L1 activation and retrotransposition are restricted to specific cell types and genomic loci.
L1HS BIO_RELATION Cancer (L1HS mobilization in somatic tissues contributes to diseases such as cancer.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Carcinoma (Some LINE-1 loci can escape DNA methylation and become active, particularly in carcinomas.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Colorectal cancer (Certain colorectal cancers were excessively mutagenized by human-specific L1s.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Disturbed spermatogenesis (Hypomethylation in L1HS was detected in disturbed spermatogenesis.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genetic disease (L1HS activity has the potential to cause disease.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genetic disease (L1Hs retrotransposition occasionally leads to human genetic disorders.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Lung cancer (Hypomethylation of LINE-1 promoters in circulating DNA of lung cancer patients is more pronounced for the human-specific L1Hs family.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSQCC exhibited the highest total levels of L1HS expression.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Neural tube defect (L1Hs hypomethylation in neuronal tissues is associated with NTD pathogenesis.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Non-small cell lung cancer (Hypomethylation of LINE-1 promoters was assessed in circulating DNA of non-small cell lung cancer patients.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Schizophrenia (L1HS transpositions are implicated as a genomic risk factor for schizophrenia.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Systemic lupus erythematosu (L1Hs loci are transcriptionally active in SLE neutrophils.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CDH11 (CDH11 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CHRM3 (L1HS provides a novel promoter for CHRM3.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CHRM3 (L1HS integrated into the CHRM3 gene.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genes associated with neural functions and disease (L1Hs elements integrate preferentially into genes associated with neural functions and diseases.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION ODZ3 (ODZ3 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION PCM1 (PCM1 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION PTPRM (PTPRM was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION ROBO2 (ROBO2 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS has a top expression context in normal_tissue: prostate gland.
L1HS has a top expression context in normal_cell_line: foreskin fibroblast.
L1HS has a top expression context in cancer_cell_line: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma.
L1HS has a representative genomic locus at chr1:231646101-231652225 with 1620 total hits.
L1HS maps to a Repbase-backed sequence record with a consensus length of 6064 bp and structure hints including LTR, LINE.
Citation Resolver normalized and deduplicated 23 citation records.

supported_claims: Resolved the TE entity L1HS with 2 strict alias variants.
Searched PubMed with the query ""L1HS" AND "expression" AND "sequence"".
Literature evidence includes "Antisense promoter of human L1 retrotransposon drives transcription of adjacent cellular genes." (PMID 11238933).
Literature evidence includes "Identification, characterization, and cell specificity of a human LINE-1 promoter." (PMID 1701022).
Literature evidence includes "Genome-Wide Young L1 Methylation Profiling by bs-ATLAS-seq." (PMID 36449162).
Literature evidence includes "Activation of individual L1 retrotransposon instances is restricted to cell-type dependent permissive loci." (PMID 27016617).
Literature evidence includes "Molecular characterization and tissue-specific expression of a murine putative G-protein-coupled receptor." (PMID 9714732).
Human L1 retrotransposon transcription is regulated by its promoter and influenced by transcription factors and environmental agents.
Young L1 elements are subject to DNA methylation, which plays a role in their silencing.
L1 activation and retrotransposition are restricted to specific cell types and genomic loci.
L1HS BIO_RELATION Cancer (L1HS mobilization in somatic tissues contributes to diseases such as cancer.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Carcinoma (Some LINE-1 loci can escape DNA methylation and become active, particularly in carcinomas.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Colorectal cancer (Certain colorectal cancers were excessively mutagenized by human-specific L1s.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Disturbed spermatogenesis (Hypomethylation in L1HS was detected in disturbed spermatogenesis.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genetic disease (L1HS activity has the potential to cause disease.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genetic disease (L1Hs retrotransposition occasionally leads to human genetic disorders.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Lung cancer (Hypomethylation of LINE-1 promoters in circulating DNA of lung cancer patients is more pronounced for the human-specific L1Hs family.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSQCC exhibited the highest total levels of L1HS expression.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Neural tube defect (L1Hs hypomethylation in neuronal tissues is associated with NTD pathogenesis.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Non-small cell lung cancer (Hypomethylation of LINE-1 promoters was assessed in circulating DNA of non-small cell lung cancer patients.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Schizophrenia (L1HS transpositions are implicated as a genomic risk factor for schizophrenia.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Systemic lupus erythematosu (L1Hs loci are transcriptionally active in SLE neutrophils.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CDH11 (CDH11 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CHRM3 (L1HS provides a novel promoter for CHRM3.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CHRM3 (L1HS integrated into the CHRM3 gene.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genes associated with neural functions and disease (L1Hs elements integrate preferentially into genes associated with neural functions and diseases.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION ODZ3 (ODZ3 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION PCM1 (PCM1 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION PTPRM (PTPRM was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION ROBO2 (ROBO2 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS has a top expression context in normal_tissue: prostate gland.
L1HS has a top expression context in normal_cell_line: foreskin fibroblast.
L1HS has a top expression context in cancer_cell_line: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma.
L1HS has a representative genomic locus at chr1:231646101-231652225 with 1620 total hits.
L1HS maps to a Repbase-backed sequence record with a consensus length of 6064 bp and structure hints including LTR, LINE.
Citation Resolver normalized and deduplicated 23 citation records.

walk_steps.summary: Resolved the TE entity L1HS with 2 strict alias variants.
Searched PubMed with the query ""L1HS" AND "expression" AND "sequence"".
Literature evidence includes "Antisense promoter of human L1 retrotransposon drives transcription of adjacent cellular genes." (PMID 11238933).
Literature evidence includes "Identification, characterization, and cell specificity of a human LINE-1 promoter." (PMID 1701022).
Literature evidence includes "Genome-Wide Young L1 Methylation Profiling by bs-ATLAS-seq." (PMID 36449162).
Literature evidence includes "Activation of individual L1 retrotransposon instances is restricted to cell-type dependent permissive loci." (PMID 27016617).
Literature evidence includes "Molecular characterization and tissue-specific expression of a murine putative G-protein-coupled receptor." (PMID 9714732).
Human L1 retrotransposon transcription is regulated by its promoter and influenced by transcription factors and environmental agents.
Young L1 elements are subject to DNA methylation, which plays a role in their silencing.
L1 activation and retrotransposition are restricted to specific cell types and genomic loci.
L1HS BIO_RELATION Cancer (L1HS mobilization in somatic tissues contributes to diseases such as cancer.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Carcinoma (Some LINE-1 loci can escape DNA methylation and become active, particularly in carcinomas.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Colorectal cancer (Certain colorectal cancers were excessively mutagenized by human-specific L1s.)

events.message:
# Research Report: L1HS Transposable Element

## Question Scope
This report examines the L1HS transposable element across five dimensions: sequence, genomic location, expression, disease associations, and supporting literature evidence. The goal is to inventory the available evidence, assess its quality, and synthesize a concise answer while transparently noting limitations and gaps.

## Evidence Inventory
Evidence was gathered from eight plugins—Entity Resolver, Literature, Literature Reading, Graph, Expression, Genome, Sequence, and Citation Resolver—producing 36 claims supported by 36 evidence items and 377 citations. Claim-level support is summarized below, grouped thematically with inline references.

### Entity Resolution
The TE entity L1HS was resolved with two strict aliases (L1HS, L1HS‑Ta) at confidence 0.93 (evidence_1).

### Sequence Information
L1HS maps to a Repbase‑backed consensus sequence of 6064 bp with structural hints including LTR and LINE (evidence_35; Repbase references by Smit et al. 1995 and Jurka & Gentles 2005).

### Genomic Location
A representative genomic locus on chromosome 1 (chr1:231646101‑231652225, minus strand, length 6124 bp) was identified, with 1620 total genomic hits (evidence_34).  
*Note: This is a representative region; L1HS is a multicopy element with numerous genomic copies.*

### Expression Profiles
Top expression contexts are: normal tissue – prostate gland (evidence_31); normal cell line – foreskin fibroblast (evidence_32); cancer cell line – anaplastic large cell lymphoma (evidence_33). These derive from precomputed aggregated expression data, not raw experimental measurements.

### Literature Evidence

#### Transcription Regulation
Human L1 retrotransposon transcription is regulated by its promoter and influenced by transcription factors and environmental agents (evidence_8; high). This integrates findings from multiple studies:
- An antisense promoter within L1 drives transcription of adjacent cellular genes (PMID 11238933).
- The human LINE‑1 promoter was identified and characterized with cell‑type specificity (PMID 1701022).
- The transcription factor RUNX3 plays a role in L1 transcription and retrotransposition (PMID 12907736).
- Steroid hormone‑like agents affect L1 transcription (PMID 11971989).

#### DNA Methylation and Silencing
Young L1 elements undergo DNA methylation, contributing to their silencing (evidence_9; medium). This is supported by a genome‑wide methylation profiling method for young L1 elements (bs‑ATLAS‑seq; PMID 36449162).

#### Cell‑Type and Locus Restriction
L1 activation and retrotransposition are restricted to specific cell types and permissive genomic loci (evidence_10; medium). The seminal study (PMID 27016617) shows that activation of individual L1 instances is cell‑type and locus dependent.

#### Off‑Target Retrieval
The PubMed search also returned a murine study (PMID 9714732) on tissue‑specific expression of a G‑protein‑coupled receptor; its relevance to human L1HS is minimal and it is noted only for completeness.

### Disease Links (Graph Plugin)
The internal knowledge graph associates L1HS with multiple diseases (all rated “high” support). Selected associations with representative supporting PMIDs are listed below; each claim is backed by multiple citations from the graph.

| Disease Association | Evidence ID | Representative PMID(s) |
|---------------------|-------------|------------------------|
| Cancer (somatic mobilization contributes to cancer) | evidence_11 | 22968929, 25352549 |

walk_steps.summary: Resolved the TE entity L1HS with 2 strict alias variants.
Searched PubMed with the query ""L1HS" AND "expression" AND "sequence"".
Literature evidence includes "Antisense promoter of human L1 retrotransposon drives transcription of adjacent cellular genes." (PMID 11238933).
Literature evidence includes "Identification, characterization, and cell specificity of a human LINE-1 promoter." (PMID 1701022).
Literature evidence includes "Genome-Wide Young L1 Methylation Profiling by bs-ATLAS-seq." (PMID 36449162).
Literature evidence includes "Activation of individual L1 retrotransposon instances is restricted to cell-type dependent permissive loci." (PMID 27016617).
Literature evidence includes "Molecular characterization and tissue-specific expression of a murine putative G-protein-coupled receptor." (PMID 9714732).
Human L1 retrotransposon transcription is regulated by its promoter and influenced by transcription factors and environmental agents.
Young L1 elements are subject to DNA methylation, which plays a role in their silencing.
L1 activation and retrotransposition are restricted to specific cell types and genomic loci.
L1HS BIO_RELATION Cancer (L1HS mobilization in somatic tissues contributes to diseases such as cancer.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Carcinoma (Some LINE-1 loci can escape DNA methylation and become active, particularly in carcinomas.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Colorectal cancer (Certain colorectal cancers were excessively mutagenized by human-specific L1s.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Disturbed spermatogenesis (Hypomethylation in L1HS was detected in disturbed spermatogenesis.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genetic disease (L1HS activity has the potential to cause disease.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genetic disease (L1Hs retrotransposition occasionally leads to human genetic disorders.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Lung cancer (Hypomethylation of LINE-1 promoters in circulating DNA of lung cancer patients is more pronounced for the human-specific L1Hs family.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSQCC exhibited the highest total levels of L1HS expression.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Neural tube defect (L1Hs hypomethylation in neuronal tissues is associated with NTD pathogenesis.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Non-small cell lung cancer (Hypomethylation of LINE-1 promoters was assessed in circulating DNA of non-small cell lung cancer patients.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Schizophrenia (L1HS transpositions are implicated as a genomic risk factor for schizophrenia.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Systemic lupus erythematosu (L1Hs loci are transcriptionally active in SLE neutrophils.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CDH11 (CDH11 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CHRM3 (L1HS provides a novel promoter for CHRM3.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION CHRM3 (L1HS integrated into the CHRM3 gene.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION Genes associated with neural functions and disease (L1Hs elements integrate preferentially into genes associated with neural functions and diseases.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION ODZ3 (ODZ3 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION PCM1 (PCM1 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION PTPRM (PTPRM was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS BIO_RELATION ROBO2 (ROBO2 was targeted by somatic LINE-1 insertions in colorectal tumors.)
L1HS has a top expression context in normal_tissue: prostate gland.
L1HS has a top expression context in normal_cell_line: foreskin fibroblast.
L1HS has a top expression context in cancer_cell_line: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma.
L1HS has a representative genomic locus at chr1:231646101-231652225 with 1620 total hits.
L1HS maps to a Repbase-backed sequence record with a consensus length of 6064 bp and structure hints including LTR, LINE.
Citation Resolver normalized and deduplicated 23 citation records.
